author: pelican state news
title: ULM baseball to host Troy for final regular season series starting May 14
text:
The University of Louisiana Monroe baseball team will conclude its regular season at home by hosting Troy, beginning Thursday, May 14. The three-game series will take place at Lou St. Amant Field and is set to wrap up on Saturday, May 16. All games will be available for streaming with live statistics provided on ULMWarhawks.com/Stats.
This matchup marks the 54th through 56th meetings between the Warhawks and Trojans since their first contest in 2007. Troy leads the all-time series with a record of 38-15, including a notable advantage when playing in Monroe. The last time these teams played at ULM’s home field was in 2024, when the Warhawks managed to win one out of three games. ULM has not secured a series victory over Troy since winning back-to-back home sets in 2015 and 2016.
Troy enters this weekend tied for fourth place in the Sun Belt Conference with an overall record identical to ULM’s (26-26), but holding a stronger conference mark at 15-12. The Trojans have claimed conference series wins against Old Dominion, Arkansas State, Texas State, Ragin’ Cajuns, Marshall and South Alabama this year. Offensively, Jimmy Janicki leads Troy with a .353 batting average along with team highs in home runs (16) and runs batted in (68).
The Warhawks are coming off a road series against Marshall where they dropped two out of three games but closed strong with a win behind performances from Bryce Blaser—who hit .500 over the weekend—and key contributions from Davis Mauzy and Jake Haggard who each drove in five runs.
Several Warhawk players have stood out this season: Davis Mauzy leads the team batting .361 with hits recorded in most games; Kade Dupont was named as a Brooks Wallace Player of the Year semifinalist thanks to his consistent offensive production (.353 average) and strong defensive play; Marcus Aranda has emerged as one of the top power hitters both on his team and within the conference.
Saturday’s game will also serve as Senior Day for ULM baseball as it recognizes fifteen seniors playing their final regular season game at Lou St. Amant Field.
